findings.body: The finally block marks the failed item complete, allowing the commit thread to commit its Kafka offset and permanently skip processing that result on restart.
findings.failure_mode: Failed result handling is acknowledged as successful and becomes unrecoverable once the offset is committed.
findings.impact: The finally block marks the failed item complete, allowing the commit thread to commit its Kafka offset and permanently skip processing that result on restart.
findings.root_cause: Offset completion is unconditional in the worker finally block, including the exception path.
findings.suggested_fix: Only call complete_offset after a successful processor invocation; retain failed work as outstanding or route it through an explicit retry/DLQ policy before acknowledging it.
findings.title: Do not acknowledge offsets when the result processor raises
findings.trigger: A result_processor invocation raises, for example because a database or downstream service operation fails after the item has been dequeued.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 149 shows complete_offset is called in finally block unconditionally after result_processor runs. pr.body:
One potential problem we have with batch processing is that any one slow item will clog up the whole batch. This pr implements a queueing method instead, where we keep N queues that each have their own workers. There's still a chance of individual items backlogging a queue, but we can try increased concurrency here to reduce the chances of that happening

<!-- Describe your PR here. -->
pr.title: feat(uptime): Add ability to use queues to manage parallelism

raw_findings.body: Queue.put never blocks because the queues have the default unbounded size, so the consumer continues accepting messages until process memory is exhausted rather than applying backpressure.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Backlogs grow without limit in process memory and can terminate the consumer under sustained slow processing.
raw_findings.impact: Queue.put never blocks because the queues have the default unbounded size, so the consumer continues accepting messages until process memory is exhausted rather than applying backpressure.
raw_findings.root_cause: The fixed queue pool creates unbounded Queue instances despite relying on queues for flow control.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Give each queue a finite maxsize (configurable if necessary) and let submit block or otherwise pause intake when that limit is reached.
raw_findings.title: Bound each work queue to provide the promised backpressure
raw_findings.trigger: The consumer receives results faster than a worker can process them, such as when a downstream database call stalls for one subscription while Kafka intake continues.

raw_findings.body: The finally block marks the failed item complete, allowing the commit thread to commit its Kafka offset and permanently skip processing that result on restart.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Failed result handling is acknowledged as successful and becomes unrecoverable once the offset is committed.
raw_findings.impact: The finally block marks the failed item complete, allowing the commit thread to commit its Kafka offset and permanently skip processing that result on restart.
raw_findings.root_cause: Offset completion is unconditional in the worker finally block, including the exception path.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Only call complete_offset after a successful processor invocation; retain failed work as outstanding or route it through an explicit retry/DLQ policy before acknowledging it.
raw_findings.title: Do not acknowledge offsets when the result processor raises
raw_findings.trigger: A result_processor invocation raises, for example because a database or downstream service operation fails after the item has been dequeued.

raw_findings.body: Once the in-flight item returns, the worker exits at the while-condition instead of fetching the remaining queued items. Those results are abandoned during the purported graceful shutdown and will at best be replayed later from Kafka.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Graceful shutdown stops consumption with queued work still unprocessed.
raw_findings.impact: Once the in-flight item returns, the worker exits at the while-condition instead of fetching the remaining queued items. Those results are abandoned during the purported graceful shutdown and will at best be replayed later from Kafka.
raw_findings.root_cause: The worker loop tests a shutdown flag before every get, and shutdown sets that flag before closing the queues.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Do not set the worker exit flag before draining. Shut down puts, allow workers to keep calling get until Queue.shutdown(immediate=False) raises ShutDown after the queue drains, then join them.
raw_findings.title: Drain queues before causing workers to exit during shutdown
raw_findings.trigger: Shutdown starts while a worker is processing one item and additional items remain queued for that worker.

raw_findings.body: A negative value creates no queues; every submitted message then raises IndexError while selecting self.queues[0], is caught by the strategy, and is marked complete and committed without invoking the result processor.
raw_findings.evidence: num_queues=max_workers or 20,  # Number of parallel queues
raw_findings.failure_mode: Invalid CLI configuration silently drops all results instead of failing startup with a configuration error.
raw_findings.impact: A negative value creates no queues; every submitted message then raises IndexError while selecting self.queues[0], is caught by the strategy, and is marked complete and committed without invoking the result processor.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new mode forwards an unvalidated integer to the queue count, while zero/negative values are not rejected.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Validate max_workers as a positive integer before constructing FixedQueuePool, and pass the validated value rather than using truthiness fallback.
raw_findings.title: Reject non-positive --max-workers for queue mode
raw_findings.trigger: The newly supported mode is started with a negative --max-workers value, which Click accepts because the option is an unconstrained integer.

raw_findings.body: join ignores its timeout and calls close, which can wait five seconds for the commit thread and then five seconds per worker (up to 20 workers by default), delaying shutdown far beyond the caller's deadline.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The consumer lifecycle cannot enforce its shutdown timeout and may hang for roughly 100 seconds with the default queue count.
raw_findings.impact: join ignores its timeout and calls close, which can wait five seconds for the commit thread and then five seconds per worker (up to 20 workers by default), delaying shutdown far beyond the caller's deadline.
raw_findings.root_cause: The join implementation discards its timeout parameter and delegates to a fixed-timeout close operation.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Implement join using the supplied timeout as a shared deadline and pass remaining time to the commit-thread and worker joins; make close use the same bounded shutdown path.
raw_findings.title: Honor the ProcessingStrategy join timeout
raw_findings.trigger: Arroyo calls join with a finite timeout while one or more result processors are blocked or slow.

raw_findings.body: The defaultdict is mutated without a shared map lock while its keys are iterated, which can raise RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration; the commit loop logs the error and skips that commit cycle.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Concurrent partition assignment/input can cause transient commit-loop failures and delayed offset commits.
raw_findings.impact: The defaultdict is mutated without a shared map lock while its keys are iterated, which can raise RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration; the commit loop logs the error and skips that commit cycle.
raw_findings.root_cause: Only per-partition contents are locked; creation and iteration of the shared partition dictionaries are unsynchronized.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Protect partition_locks and the all_offsets key snapshot with a pool-level lock, or maintain a lock-protected partition set and snapshot it before per-partition processing.
raw_findings.title: Synchronize the partition map while taking commit snapshots
raw_findings.trigger: The commit thread snapshots all_offsets while submit is adding the first offset for a newly assigned partition.

raw_findings.body: The pool workers are stopped, but each SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy's daemon commit thread is never signaled and continues to retain the strategy, queue pool, and commit callback indefinitely.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Shutdown leaks background commit threads and can leave stale commit callbacks active after the factory is disposed.
raw_findings.impact: The pool workers are stopped, but each SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy's daemon commit thread is never signaled and continues to retain the strategy, queue pool, and commit callback indefinitely.
raw_findings.root_cause: Factory.shutdown only shuts down the queue pool and has no path to set the strategy's shutdown_event.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Track the queue strategy created by the factory and close it from shutdown, or give the shared pool a shutdown event that strategy commit loops observe and exit on.
raw_findings.title: Stop queue-strategy commit threads from factory shutdown
raw_findings.trigger: A caller follows the factory shutdown API after creating a thread-queue-parallel strategy but does not separately call that strategy's close method.

raw_findings.body: The test fails intermittently even when consistent hashing is implemented correctly; with uniform hashes the chance that at least one of three buckets is absent in 20 samples is nonzero.
raw_findings.failure_mode: CI gains a hash-seed-dependent flaky test unrelated to product correctness.
raw_findings.impact: The test fails intermittently even when consistent hashing is implemented correctly; with uniform hashes the chance that at least one of three buckets is absent in 20 samples is nonzero.
raw_findings.root_cause: The test assumes a finite random-hash sample must occupy every bucket.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Construct keys by searching for one that maps to each queue index, then assert those selected keys cover the indices, or only assert that returned indices are valid for this random sample.
raw_findings.title: Avoid probabilistic queue-distribution assertion
raw_findings.trigger: A Python hash seed maps the 20 selected group strings to only one or two of the three queue indices.

Factory shutdown doesn't call strategy.close(), but the strategy is created per create_with_partitions call and Arroyo lifecycle should call close(). This is speculative about lifecycle misuse.

validated_findings.body: The test fails intermittently even when consistent hashing is implemented correctly; with uniform hashes the chance that at least one of three buckets is absent in 20 samples is nonzero.
validated_findings.failure_mode: CI gains a hash-seed-dependent flaky test unrelated to product correctness.
validated_findings.impact: The test fails intermittently even when consistent hashing is implemented correctly; with uniform hashes the chance that at least one of three buckets is absent in 20 samples is nonzero.
validated_findings.root_cause: The test assumes a finite random-hash sample must occupy every bucket.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Construct keys by searching for one that maps to each queue index, then assert those selected keys cover the indices, or only assert that returned indices are valid for this random sample.
validated_findings.title: Avoid probabilistic queue-distribution assertion
validated_findings.trigger: A Python hash seed maps the 20 selected group strings to only one or two of the three queue indices.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 106 asserts len(queue_indices)==3 after hashing 20 group strings to 3 queues. With hash randomization (PYTHONHASHSEED), the distribution of 20 items into 3 buckets may not cover all 3 buckets. The birthday problem shows ~14% chance of missing at least one bucket. This creates a flaky test.
